text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty: DB/Redis alert fired for service=runtime-cache (pd_incident=PD-78901). symptom=redis maxclients error + connection backlog > 95% across redis-cluster-prod-2. page severity=critical. docs: https://redwood.internal/ops/runbooks/redis-saturation
PagerDuty: Auto-escalation in 5m if unacked.
alex_oncall: Acked (PD-78901). I'm on it, pulling logs and metrics.
alex_oncall: Observed spike in client count on shard-2: maxclients=10000, used=9900, connections waiting (client-output-buffer) increasing. Some 503s upstream.
maria_sre: saw similar trend in dashboards. latency for /embed endpoint jumping from 60ms -> 800ms concurrently. Likely connection exhaustion, not eviction.
alex_oncall: Running quick `redis-cli -h shard-2 info clients` and `CLIENT LIST | wc -l` now. Suspecting a retry storm from api-worker pool.
ops-bot: automated note: deployment tag `canary/worker-1623` rolled 03:12 UTC. Related logs: `worker reconnect loop` increased after rollout.
alex_oncall: Rolling back canary not yet — want to confirm. Paging app team. @dan_product can you confirm any recent changes to client libraries or connection pooling?
dan_product: We pushed a small change to SDK: switched to persistent connections with higher concurrency. Rolling back now because that matches timing. Sorry, doing rollback now :grimacing:.
maria_sre: Meanwhile we need immediate mitigation. Options: 1) Increase `maxclients` on shard-2, 2) Temporarily disable some API routes, 3) Scale up a read-only fallback, 4) Restart redis process (risky). Thoughts?
alex_oncall: I'm going to increase maxclients by 25% on shard-2 as a short-term relief and rate-limit /embed on the edge. Applying config via Ansible: ```ansible-playbook playbooks/redis-maxclients.yml -e redis_host=shard-2 -e maxclients=12500```
incident-bot: action: runbook step executed by alex_oncall: updated config, reloaded redis.
alex_oncall: Config applied, reloaded. CLIENT LIST now shows used=7600. backpressure reduced. Error rate down ~6% -> 1.2%.
maria_sre: Great. Can we coordinate a full handoff in 15m? I'll take the next 2 hour window to monitor and validate.
PagerDuty: PD-78901 acknowledged by alex_oncall at 4123456790. Auto-escalation cancelled.
alex_oncall: Noted. We'll still rollback the SDK change per dan_product. Dan: confirm when rollback completes so we can drain any leftover connections.
dan_product: Rollback started 03:28 UTC, rollback complete 03:31 UTC. Logs show old behavior resumed.
maria_sre: I'm starting a slow drain of connections from the worker fleet: `kubectl rollout pause deployment/worker && kubectl patch` then resume with backoff. Will post progress.
alex_oncall: FYI I patched the edge rate limiter to 30% throttle for /embed and /batch-embeds to reduce client churn.
ops-bot: metric-snapshot: redis_shard2_active_clients=7650 -> 3000 over 8m after throttles and rollback. latency stable.
maria_sre: Customer impact: small spike in 502/503 for ~8 minutes concentrated on embed-heavy customers. CS ticket queued. No broad data loss.
dan_product: I'm coordinating with Growth (rolling notification) and will follow up with a postmortem root cause: misconfigured persistent-connections + no client-side backoff.
alex_oncall: Handoff to maria_sre at 4123456815 — continuing monitoring and starting incident report. Leaving recovery notes in runbook.
maria_sre: Taking over monitoring. Next steps: harden worker SDK connection pooling defaults, add Redis client semaphore in runtime, add alert for connection wait queue depth.
alex_oncall: Thanks all. Closing PD once stable for 30min. :white_check_mark:
incident-bot: PD-78901 status changed to resolved by alex_oncall at 4123456820 (duration ~5m).
